f111v-112r.summary: Camus to Villeroy from Castets, 21 March 1586: the old carrier to 'le parent', the secret contact, can no longer help; Camus asks for orders for the service of 'the lord you know of'.
f111v-112r.en: I wrote to the bearer by a man sent expressly, and while awaiting the answer; but since the relative is no longer in this country, I find myself much at a loss how to govern myself, for the said bearer can no longer help me, nor even get me seen. Command what you judge best, and for the service of the lord you know of, and you will be obeyed and served as you prescribe, for I [?] you [?] [?]

f132v.summary: Castets, 1 April 1586: phrases about the bearer and the 'poursuivant'; no contemporary decipherment.

f134v.summary: Bordeaux, early April 1586: seeing the bearer, something to be presented to the 'poursuivant'; the margin paraphrases.

f151r.summary: Bordeaux, 12 April 1586: seeing the bearer is Camus's excuse to arrange 'la partie que scauez', which he hopes will be carried out on Monday without suspicion.
f151r.en: It is my excuse for having the opportunity of seeing the bearer and arranging the matter you know of, which I hope will be carried out on Monday and without [?suspicion].

f272.summary: La Rochelle, June 1586: men sent to see Camus about their part with 'le parent', without telling him anything particular; Camus asks to be relieved and withdrawn.

system: Letter cipher of invented and Latin-like signs with homophones for the letters, some signs carrying two or three values, word signs (de, la, le, qui/que, et, pour/par, vous, car) and nulls, written as blocks inside clear letters (Tomokiyo's table, corrected…
